content:
maya: Heads-up — opened a tiny TF change to add a capacity reservation + spot fallback policy for the gpu nodepool. Can someone eyeball the secrets wiring and taint/toleration bits before I merge?

maya: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/terraform/compare/fe2 -> adds module.gpu_pool.capacity_reservation_id and spot_fallback = true

maya: Terraform snippet (added vars):
```hcl
variable \"capacity_reservation_id\" { type = string, default = \"\" }
module \"gpu_pool\" {
  source = \"../../modules/gpu-pool\"
  instance_types = var.instance_types
  capacity_reservation_id = var.capacity_reservation_id
  spot_fallback = var.spot_fallback
}
```

sam: Quick q — where is capacity_reservation created? Is that a separate TF resource per AZ or managed by cloud ops?

maya: It's created in cloud-ops/aws-reservations (separate stack). Here we just reference the reservation id so the nodepool attaches to it when not using spot. If var empty -> nodepool uses on-demand profile only.

jin: Small kube note: if we attach reservation across 3 AZs make sure the node labels match our nodeAffinity. Otherwise pods might schedule unevenly. Also need toleration for the taint we add: `dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule`

lia: Also confirm the KMS key path for node boot secrets. The module reads `secrets.kms_key_arn` from SSM param `/infra/gpu/kms_arn`. Did you validate the IAM role has kms:Decrypt?

maya: Yep IAM role `tf-nodepool-provisioner` has kms:Decrypt on the key. But the PR currently wires the SSM name as plaintext: `ssm_parameter = "/infra/gpu/kms_arn"` — thinking to switch to using SSM:GetParameter with `withDecryption=true` at provision time. Thoughts?

sam: That's fine but prefer storing the full ARN in TF var for enterprise accounts. SSM name is ok for dev, but prod should be explicit. Add a note in the module docstring.

jin: For preemptible/spot eviction: make sure the nodepool has the kubelet flag `--eviction-hard=memory.available<100Mi,nodefs.available<10%`? But more importantly, add a `pod-disruption-budget` for critical workloads and a `preemptible-drain` daemonset to cordon+drain within 30s of termination notice. We have the script in ops/runbooks/preemptible-drain.sh

maya: Good call. I added `lifecycle.preemptible_termination_handler = true` in module input which deploys the daemonset. PR includes reference to that script.

lia: One more: the taint key should be `redwood.com/gpu-reserved` to avoid colliding with other infra. Example toleration in deployment: 
```yaml
- key: \"redwood.com/gpu-reserved\"
  operator: \"Exists\"
  effect: \"NoSchedule\"
```

maya: Updated the PR to use that taint key and added nodeSelector `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: h100` for our heavy batches. Also added fallback instance_types order: [h100, a10g, t4] so spot fallback chooses cheaper supported GPU.

sam: tiny nit: prefer `instance.kubernetes.io/instance-type` label (k8s standard). Otherwise LGTM.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: CI checks passed: `terraform plan` ok, `kube-lint` warnings: missing PDB for namespace 'inference' — see CI artifacts: https://ci.redwood/jobs/4321/artifacts

maya: thanks — will add a PDB and address the label nit. merging after that.

jin: happy to pair on a follow-up to validate the reservation attach in staging once merged.

maya: awesome, ping me when you're free and I'll run the staging bootstrap. :thumbsup:
